title: Draft a Report Summary
description: Write an executive summary and findings section based on a simulated forensic timeline.
problemStatement:
**Scenario:** You have completed analysis of an intellectual property theft case. Below is a simplified timeline of key events derived from evidence (laptop, email, server logs):

- 2026-02-10 09:15: Engineer logged into company laptop.
- 2026-02-10 09:30: Inserted a personal USB drive (serial 123ABC).
- 2026-02-10 09:35: Copied 'ProjectX_Source.zip' (containing trade secrets) to the USB.
- 2026-02-10 09:40: Sent email from company account to personal@gmail.com with subject "Project X backup" and attachment ProjectX_Source.zip.
- 2026-02-10 10:00: Cleared browser history and deleted email from sent items.
- 2026-02-10 10:15: Removed USB drive.

The USB drive was recovered at the engineer's home and contained the zip file. Email logs from Office 365 confirm the email even though it was deleted from the client.

Your task: **Write an executive summary (2-3 paragraphs) and a findings section (bullet points)** suitable for a corporate management report. Remember to:
- Separate facts from any opinion.
- Use clear, non-technical language.
- Reference evidence items (e.g., USB S/N 123ABC, email logs).
- Provide a concise conclusion of what happened.
hints: Executive summary: start with the allegation, then state the conclusion based on evidence.
Findings: each bullet should be a factual statement linked to evidence.
If you include an opinion (e.g., 'the engineer intentionally exfiltrated data'), label it clearly as expert opinion.
expectedOutput: A well-structured executive summary and findings section in plain English.
solutionCode:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
An investigation was conducted into allegations that former engineer [Name] improperly transferred proprietary source code prior to termination. Digital forensic analysis of the company-issued laptop, recovered USB drive, and Office 365 email records established that on February 10, 2026, the engineer copied a file containing trade secrets to a personal USB device and sent the same file to an external personal email account. These actions appear to have been intentional and were followed by efforts to erase local traces of the activity.

FINDINGS
- At 09:15 on 2026-02-10, the engineer logged into their company laptop (evidence: Windows event log entry #104).
- At 09:30, a personal USB drive (SanDisk, S/N 123ABC) was connected (evidence: USB connection log, registry key).
- At 09:35, the file 'ProjectX_Source.zip' (containing proprietary code) was copied to the USB drive (evidence: file system MAC times and LNK file).
- At 09:40, an email was sent from the engineer's corporate account to personal@gmail.com, with the same file attached (evidence: Office 365 message trace and email export).
- At 10:00, the engineer deleted the sent email and cleared the browser history on the laptop (evidence: deletion artifacts in email database and browser history carving).
- At 10:15, the USB drive was removed.
- The USB drive was later recovered and was found to contain the 'ProjectX_Source.zip' file (evidence: forensic image of USB, hash match with original internal repository file).

EXPERT OPINION
Based on the totality of the evidence, it is my professional opinion that the engineer deliberately transferred sensitive company intellectual property to an unauthorized external location and personal device, and took steps to cover their tracks. No evidence was found to suggest the transfer was accidental or for legitimate business purposes.
